evidence.scenarioScope: Administrator can disable an account.
evidence.rationale: Independent integration mapping from explicitly reviewed operation assertions, not inferred from scenario tags or aggregate suite names.
assertionDetails: A real bootstrap administrator successfully disables Bob while unrelated Charlie receives403 for the same admin action; original IRC/event sessions close, old REST/login credentials fail, durable disabled state and intended/private event isolation survive recreation.

Before disable, Bob's separately authenticated IRC and event sockets publish/receive a real private-channel control; ordinary Charlie cannot disable Bob (403), and the original IRC socket is still OPEN before rootadmin acts.

Rootadmin was created through the genuine bootstrap registration/login flow; admin disable returns exactly 200. The original IRC and event sockets close; an attempted send uses that original connection if still OPEN after the HTTP response.
Existing REST credential send and subsequent read return exactly 401, and login with Bob's actual password remains 401 after restart.

Alice's post-disable private message reaches her member event stream but neither Bob's old IRC/event socket nor Charlie's unrelated stream; disabled-publish reaches no channel recipient and is absent from REST history/SQLite.

SQLite stores Bob disabled_at, Alice still enabled, Bob original content and Alice new private row with correct authors; unrelated private history and channel custom-role assignments remain unchanged; recreated runtime retains new content and rejects Bob.

evidence.testTitle: MSG-027: disabled authority is rechecked on surviving sockets despite lost invalidation delivery
evidence.scenarioScope: Account disable revokes active access.
evidence.rationale: Independent integration mapping from explicitly reviewed operation assertions, not inferred from scenario tags or aggregate suite names.
assertionDetails: Disable commits with eager invalidation deliberately lost; original sockets are assertedOPEN and submit a forbidden frame without a conditional skip, production ingress rechecks authoritative account state and closes1000, no protected output or mutation occurs, and disabled authority stays revoked after recreation.

All users and rootadmin are provisioned through genuine public registration/bootstrap/login on the frozen production runtime with unique passwords; original credentials and SQLite directory are reused by a copied-bundle Miniflare fixture.

Both original Bob sockets are unconditionally asserted OPEN after committed disable; the original sender unconditionally sends PRIVMSG disabled-surviving-socket-publish and the unchanged production ingress check closes it with code 1000/reason Account no longer available.

Existing Bob REST append is exactly 401; Alice private post still reaches authorized IRC/event recipients, while Bob receiver/event stream and unrelated Charlie IRC/event stream receive no private content and no stream receives forbidden publish content.

A second device can remain open after account-wide membership cleanup; if still OPEN its next PING triggers the unchanged credential recheck and closure, rather than assuming membership removal always immediately closes every socket.

After actual fixture disposal, SQLite contains no disabled IRC/REST publish, retains original/unrelated/Alice-new message authors and bodies, stores Bob disabled_at with Alice enabled, preserves root admin role and empty Bob/custom-channel role assignments; a new uninstrumented production runtime keeps Bob REST at 401 and retains legitimate/unrelated history.

evidence.testTitle: [DB-009 DB-010 DB-011 MSG-026 DM-017 DB-027] independent runtime restart preserves private messages, edits and redactions and rejects foreign cursors

evidence.testTitle: [DB-013 DB-014 DB-028] actual SQLite foreign keys, unique sequences and indexed bounded history queries enforce integrity
evidence.scenarioScope: Actual persisted schema constraints plus representative 120-message before-pagination/index plans.
evidence.rationale: Exact Vitest test completed; only the listed assertions are credited. Other dimensions remain required and uncovered unless another matched test covers them.
assertionDetails: Real public sends populate 120 rows; an authenticated reader receives 100 then 20 disjoint records using the oldest-ID cursor despite an extreme requested limit.
The stopped actual database rejects missing-role foreign keys, duplicate role assignments and duplicate message sequences; foreign_key_check is clean and the 120 original rows remain.
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows indexed sequence-range history and indexed user-role lookup; around/time cursor plans and production-scale load are not established.

authorization.rationale: EXPLAIN of the history/role lookup SQL is an internal query-plan inspection, not an externally authorized client operation. Live account authentication is setup, not the property established by the planner assertions.

events.rationale: EXPLAIN/query-plan inspection is read-only internal maintenance and has no recipient/event contract.

restart.rationale: The read-only planner checks immutable persisted indexes on a fresh SQLite connection. No intended stored change needs post-runtime restoration.

unrelatedResources.rationale: Read-only EXPLAIN and bounded SELECT inspect no mutable resource and have no unrelated write target; the120-row count also remains unchanged.

assertionDetails: PASS and SASL IRC fields observed: acceptList, accountName, authenticated, awayMessage, capNegotiating, capabilities, connectedAt, credentialVersion, hostname, ip, isBot, isDirectWebSocket, isOper, languages, lastActiveAt, metadataSubs, nickname, realname, registered, requestedNick, roles, saslBuffer, saslMechanism, sessionId, subprotocol, userId, userModes, username, vhost.

evidence.testTitle: sqlite 10485760 byte real upload limits MEDIA-009 MEDIA-012 ABUSE-007: oversized and exhausted quota denials are silent and inert across restart
evidence.scenarioScope: SQLite upload size and full 100 MiB quota with actual 10 MiB objects, observed denial windows and restart.
evidence.rationale: This executed case covers only the named provider, upload sizes, aliases, observer windows and state checks.
assertionDetails: Independent Alice, Bob and Charlie authenticate via public registration, login and IRC PASS; Alice and Bob join a secret channel and Charlie is outside it. SQLite stores real upload bytes in workerd persistence.

Both upload aliases reject actual 10 MiB+1 request bodies with 413 and no Location, content or UUID; filling exactly 100 MiB with 10 MiB objects succeeds, and both aliases reject further payloads with 403 without Location, payload or UUID.

Before and after each rejection, three live IRC clients and three ticket event streams receive shared-channel barriers; no additional IRC or event data is delivered in the rejection window. A test-only read-only SQLite metadata accessor and, for R2, actual bucket object listing remain identical across each denial.

Bob downloads a channel-scoped positive object with the expected SHA256 while Charlie gets 404; Bob’s independent private object remains readable. Owner deletion frees quota and permits replacement, whose bytes are checked after an independent workerd restart.

Stopped workerd SQLite metadata matches the pre-stop state, including owner, scope, sizes, storage kind and SQLite bytes length; R2 object listing remains identical after restart. A restored six-stream observer window confirms another legacy-alias quota denial is silent and inert.
SQLite stores bounded chunks with metadata and digest in one transaction; retained payload is downloaded and compared byte-for-byte via SHA256 after restart. R2 uses the real Miniflare bucket.
